sources.claim: The Open Source Initiative published the Open Source AI Definition 1.0 (October 2024). Downloadable model weights ("open weights") can still come with license terms that restrict some uses, so open weights are not automatically open source; the definition itself is disputed by some groups.

sections.skill: Explain that downloadable weights still come with license terms

questions.prompt: What are a model's weights?

choices.text: The learned numbers that make it work
How heavy the computer is that runs the model, measured in kilograms or pounds

questions.correct_answer: The learned numbers that make it work
questions.intro: A model's WEIGHTS are the learned numbers that make it work. Some developers let anyone download them, called OPEN WEIGHTS. Downloadable does not mean "no rules": open-weight models come with a LICENSE, a legal agreement that can limit COMMERCIAL use, require credit, ban certain uses, or set conditions for large companies. Open weights are also not automatically "open source"; the Open Source Initiative published an Open Source AI Definition (version 1.0, October 2024), though some groups dispute it. Before using a downloaded model for a project, read its license for your intended use.

sections.skill: Compare model licenses with a free font's terms

questions.prompt: Is the font free to download?

choices.text: No, because every font on the internet must be bought before it can be downloaded

questions.intro: A designer finds a FREE FONT online. It is free to download, but its terms say "free for personal use; buy a license for commercial use." Using it on a company's paid ads without a license breaks those terms, even though the download was free. Open-weight models work the same way: free to download does not mean free for every use. The license says what you may do.

sections.title: Apply it

sections.skill: Handle varied and changing license terms

questions.prompt: A license forbids use in products with more than a certain number of users. Why does this matter?

choices.text: A growing product might later break the terms
It does not matter, because user limits in licenses are never enforced against anyone

questions.correct_answer: A growing product might later break the terms
questions.intro: License terms vary widely. One may allow any use with credit; another may forbid use in certain products or above a number of users; another may require sharing changes. Licenses can change between versions, so read the one that comes with the exact version you download. If a project is commercial or public, or the terms are unclear, ask someone who handles legal questions. "Everyone else uses it" is not permission.
